title: Carve 0.2 escape contexts
description: The cases the writer has to test for an escape. They are not the rule: the writer decides each escape by reparsing the candidate line in its context (C2-W-089), and a backslash is written exactly when the output without it would parse to a different tree (C2-W-088). `contexts` is sorted by name.

unit.description: Where a construct opens on a run of characters, the escape is placed so that the whole run reads as text.

clauses.description: The clause ids of the six 0.2 documents that the row encodes. The row is normative together with these clauses.

name.description: The identifier of the row, unique in its list.

group.description: The clause of the list the case comes from: a block opener or interrupter, delimiter pairing, a bracket construct, a sigil form, an opening brace, a backslash in text, a table cell.

triggers.description: The characters at which the test is made. For a run, its shortest form. Empty where the case is a shape and not a fixed character.

positions.description: Where the characters must stand for the case to apply. One entry is enough. The cited clauses define each.
